subject: Immediate: inflight queue surge and streaming stalls (/v1/generate)
messages:
From: Daniel Huang <daniel.huang@edgespark.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: sustained p99 latency and 5xx spike on /v1/generate

Mina,

We're seeing a sustained p99 jump from ~180ms to 2.7s and 5xx rate up to 3.8% since ~08:50am PT. Throughput on our tenant pool has dropped ~35% despite no change in client traffic. The user-facing checkout flow is timing out for a subset of requests.

Our traces show long queuing in the serving layer and then a burst of 504s. Logs indicate many requests stuck waiting on token streaming and then timing out — looks like an inflight queue pileup. I've attached samples and graphs (influx).

Can you please escalate and confirm whether this is a KV cache/priority-lane issue or something with batching? This is hitting production payment flows. 

Attachments: influx_graphs_20261204.png (image/png), request_samples_20261204.log (text)

— Daniel
Head of Platform, EdgeSpark
daniel.huang@edgespark.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:18:45-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Immediate: sustained p99 latency and 5xx spike on /v1/generate

Forwarding EdgeSpark's report — P1. Their checkout traffic is affected. Initial read feels like a head-of-line (HOL) stall caused by a cache eviction loop or prefix-cardinality surge on their tenant's KV partition.

Ask for infra/serving team:
- Check tenant pool metrics for a spike in prefix cardinality, eviction rate, and KV miss ratio around 08:45–09:05 PT.
- Confirm if there were any recent config changes to batching windows, dynamic batch thresholds, or KV eviction aggressiveness for the pool serving EdgeSpark.
- Provide live p99, 90/95 latencies and 5xx breakdown by backend.

This needs exec visibility if it's a capacity/patch request. Attaching customer logs.

— Mina
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:24:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Immediate: sustained p99 latency and 5xx spike on /v1/generate

On Fri, 2026-12-04 at 09:18, Mina Haddad wrote:
> Forwarding EdgeSpark's report — P1.

Checked fleet telemetry (live):
- Tenant pool shows a sharp increase in prefix cardinality at ~08:48 (x6 baseline).
- KV eviction rate jumped 4x and we see repeated re-populate cycles for their prefixes (suggests mis-sized prefix cache + high interleaving of many short prefixes).
- Batch lane starvation observed: long-running HOT requests are consuming batching slots leading to HOL blocking for small, latency-sensitive requests.
- No recent global batching policy changes in last 24h; there was an A/B of adaptive batching weights rolled out to 10% earlier this week but not targeted at this pool.

Immediate mitigation suggestions (short window, low-risk):
1) Temporarily reduce batching_max_delay to 6ms for the affected pool to favor latency-sensitive flows.
2) Increase prefix-cache-size for this tenant pool by 30% and lower eviction aggressiveness for 20 minutes to break the refill loop.
3) If mitigation above fails within 10m, fail open heavy requests to a fallback smaller-model variant (lower memory) to relieve KV pressure.

I've kicked off a quick job to snapshot current cache stats and pushed a non-disruptive increase to the prefix-cache-size (change id: INF-1247-step1). Monitoring now.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:36:02-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Immediate: sustained p99 latency and 5xx spike on /v1/generate

Thanks team — good triage. I'm looping in Grace (VP Ops) for exec visibility. Two operational asks:

1) Jonas — please proceed with the reduced batching_max_delay and prefix cache size bump. Keep the change as a rolling, non-disruptive flag so we can revert quickly. Track impact on p99 and 5xx.
2) Rishi — please prepare a quick traffic routing play: if p99 does not fall below 400ms in 10m, route 25% of EdgeSpark traffic to their dedicated reserved lane (we have capacity) and enable automatic fallback to the smaller model variant for heavy requests.

We should also prepare a short customer note summarizing cause/next steps. Mina, can you own comms (ETA + mitigation) and include the ticket/JIRA link?

Executive note: potential temporary credit/SLR for customer if impact > 30 min. Grace, please advise on approval threshold.

— Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Huang <daniel.huang@edgespark.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: inflight queue surge and streaming stalls (/v1/generate)

Mina — thanks for the rapid response and for routing this up. We can see some immediate improvement after ~09:40 when your team applied the prefix-cache bump (p99 down from 2.7s to ~720ms and 5xx dropped to 1.1%). Still above baseline, but moving in the right direction.

We're happy to accept temporary routing to a reserved lane if that stabilizes checkout latency while you tune KV configs. Please keep us posted on ETA for full resolution and any rollback schedule.

I'll attach a couple of additional trace samples if helpful (sending shortly).

— Daniel
Head of Platform, EdgeSpark
daniel.huang@edgespark.com
